turns.text: Hi! What did you get for how much the travel costs, and how did you get it?
I got 200 dollars. I did 50% of 400.
Okay, 50% of 400 is the part you found. The problem says the tickets cost 50% more than the supplies, so what does "more than" tell you about the tickets compared to the supplies?
Um, that they cost more than the supplies? But I still think it's 200, since that's 50% of 400.
If the supplies cost 400 dollars and the tickets cost 200, which one is bigger?
Oh, the supplies are bigger. So the tickets can't be 200 if they cost more... I guess I have to add it to the 400.
Nice noticing. So what amount would you have for the tickets then?
Can you explain why adding the 200 to the 400 makes sense here?
Because the tickets cost the supplies plus 50% extra. So the travel cost is 600 dollars.
Exactly, the tickets are the supplies plus half of the supplies. [END]
